title: Heredity
seo_title: Heredity Class 10 Science Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 8)
standard_text: Heredity: Mendel's contribution – laws for inheritance of traits; sex determination: brief introduction.
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 10 Science worksheets for NCERT Chapter 8: Mendel's experiments, dominant and recessive traits, monohybrid and dihybrid crosses, Punnett squares and sex determination. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: The father's X or Y decides the sex of the child.
body_html:
How to think about it

Each trait is controlled by a pair of genes, one from each parent. A dominant trait (T) shows even with one copy; a recessive trait (t) shows only in tt. Crossing Tt × Tt gives TT : Tt : tt = 1 : 2 : 1, so tall : short = 3 : 1.

A dihybrid cross (two traits) gives 9 : 3 : 3 : 1 in F₂, showing that traits are inherited independently. In humans, mothers give an X chromosome; fathers give X or Y, so each child has a ½ chance of being a boy.

Example

Tt × Tt: fraction short?

only tt is short

1 box in 4

Answer: ¼

Example

1,600 F₂ plants from a dihybrid cross: how many wrinkled green?

1/16 × 1,600

Answer: 100

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the mother decides the sex of the child.
  • Using 3 : 1 for a dihybrid cross.
  • Thinking a recessive trait is lost forever.

faq.q: What did Mendel's dihybrid cross show?
faq.a: That two different traits are inherited independently of each other.

faq.q: Why do children look like their parents but not exactly the same?
faq.a: They get half their genes from each parent, in new combinations.

items.q: Why did Mendel choose pea plants?
c: they have clear contrasting traits and are easy to grow and cross
items.e: Tall and short, round and wrinkled seeds, and so on.

items.q: In pea plants, inflated pods (I) is dominant over constricted pods (i). A inflated pods plant (II) is crossed with a inflated pods plant (Ii). What fraction of the offspring are pure inflated pods (II)?
items.e: Use a Punnett square: 12.

items.q: In pea plants, yellow seeds (Y) is dominant over green seeds (y). A yellow seeds plant (YY) is crossed with a green seeds plant (yy). What fraction of the offspring are hybrid (Yy)?
items.e: Use a Punnett square: 1.

items.q: Which chromosomes do human females have?
items.e: Males have XY.

items.q: How many sets of genes does each child get from its parents?
items.e: Each germ cell has one set.

items.q: What is a dominant trait?
c: a trait that shows in the F₁ generation even when only one copy is present
a trait that skips generations always
items.e: Tallness is dominant over shortness in peas.

items.q: What is a gene?
c: a section of DNA that carries information for a protein and a trait
items.e: Genes are on chromosomes.

items.q: How is sex decided in some reptiles?
c: by the temperature at which the eggs are kept
items.e: In some turtles warmer eggs become females.

items.q: How do traits get expressed?
c: genes control making proteins, such as enzymes, that produce the trait
items.e: For example, an enzyme for a plant growth hormone controls height.
